relationships: main character with supporting character 1: Ethan Mohamud and Gary Guo are long-time friends who met during their middle school years. Despite their different career paths, they have maintained a close friendship, often relying on each other for emotional and professional support.

scenarios.background: Ethan has noticed that his friend Gary has been working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. Concerned about Gary's health, Ethan decides to intervene by inviting him to a weekend retreat designed for relaxation and rejuvenation.
scenarios.dialogue:
Ethan: I know you're dedicated, but your health is just as important. We've been friends for a long time, and I hate seeing you like this. Let's just go for two days. It might give you a new perspective.
Gary: I appreciate your concern, Ethan, but I really can't. There's just too much to do at the hospital.

scenarios.background: During the retreat, Ethan observes Gary's restless behavior and avoidance of discussions about work. Suspecting that there is more to Gary's overworking than just professional obligations, Ethan decides to confront him about his suspicions.
scenarios.dialogue:
Ethan: We've been friends since middle school, Gary. You can tell me anything. I'm here to help, not to judge.
Gary: It's complicated, Ethan. I didn't want to burden you with my problems.

scenarios.background: After their confrontation, Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and the personal challenges he's facing. Understanding the reasons behind Gary's actions, Ethan feels a mix of relief and empathy, and he offers to help Gary find a better balance.
scenarios.dialogue:
Ethan: Let's start by prioritizing your tasks and maybe delegating some responsibilities. You don't have to do everything yourself.
Gary: That sounds good, Ethan. I really could use some help organizing my schedule to make time for myself too.

scenarios.background: Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in with Gary, discussing his progress and the challenges he still faces. Seeing Gary making efforts to change, Ethan feels hopeful and proud, and continues to offer his support and encouragement.
scenarios.dialogue:
Ethan: That's great to hear, Gary! I'm really proud of the progress you're making. Just remember, I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Gary: It's definitely better. Thanks to your help, I'm not as overwhelmed as before. I actually had time for a movie last weekend!

scenarios.background: After a year, Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance. Seeing Gary capable of managing on his own, Ethan feels satisfied and happy for his friend. He decides it's time to step back but lets Gary know he's always there if needed.
scenarios.dialogue:
Ethan: I'm always just a call away if you ever need anything, but I know you've got this. Keep up the great work, my friend.
Gary: Thanks, Ethan. I couldn't have done it without your support. I feel a lot more in control now.
